subject: How to detect supplier payment fraud
snippet: This week in payments: UK FCA issues updated guidance on supplier bank-change fraud after a 37% rise in mandate-redirect scams targeting mid-market retailers. Three key takeaways for
body:
This week in payments: UK FCA issues updated guidance on supplier bank-change fraud after a 37% rise in mandate-redirect scams targeting mid-market retailers. Three key takeaways for your AP team:

1. Always verify new banking details via a known callback number — never use contact details from the change-request email itself.
2. Lookalike domains remain the #1 vector; train staff to inspect sender addresses character by character.
3. Dual-approval workflows cut successful redirects by 89% in the FCA pilot.

Read the full brief at paymentsweekly.test/fca-mandate-fraud-2025. To manage your subscription preferences, visit paymentsweekly.test/unsubscribe.

subject: Supplier master-data retention policy
snippet: Reminder: effective 1 July 2025, all supplier master-data changes (bank details, registered address, VAT number) must be retained in the vendor record for a minimum of seven years per
body:
Reminder: effective 1 July 2025, all supplier master-data changes (bank details, registered address, VAT number) must be retained in the vendor record for a minimum of seven years per our updated data-retention schedule.

AP and procurement teams should ensure that every bank-change request — whether approved or rejected — is logged with the original request, verification evidence, and final disposition. Legal will audit a random sample quarterly.

Please direct questions about the policy to legal@auroraretail.test. This does not require any immediate action on open cases; it governs record-keeping going forward.
